description:
Tracks the latest release of every tool agnix validates (one entry per tool with a validator in crates/agnix-core/src/rules/, and one entry per release line when agnix supports two lines of the same tool: `opencode` is OpenCode 1 and `opencode-v2` is OpenCode 2). `validators` lists the file stems of the crates/agnix-core/src/rules/*.rs modules that check the tool's files; shared helpers (for example mcp_servers, kiro_engine, opencode_version) and modules that run on every tool's Markdown (xml, imports, prompt, cross_platform, project_level) are not listed. Used by .github/workflows/tool-release-watch.yml to open per-tool issues when a new release is published. Untracked tools include the precise publication URL in untracked_reason so a maintainer can monitor manually.

Optional `changes_of_interest` per tool describes what agnix cares about: `config_surfaces` (files agnix validates), `relevant` (change-types that likely affect a validator), `irrelevant` (safe to skip). When set and GLM_API_KEY is available, the watcher runs scripts/glm-extract.js --mode=agnix-triage to produce a pre-filtered summary at the top of the issue body. Falls back gracefully to the full changelog on any LLM failure.

relevant: New or renamed top-level keys in settings.json / managed-settings.json
New hook event names, hook action types (command/http/prompt/agent/mcp_tool/...), or required fields per type
Changes to skill/agent frontmatter fields or validation rules
Changes to CLAUDE.md import syntax, directives, or size limits
Plugin manifest schema changes in .claude-plugin/plugin.json
MCP server config schema changes (fields, auth shapes, placeholders)
New built-in tool names (affecting the allow-list validator)
Output-style or rules-file schema changes
Marketplace schema changes in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (fields, source types, reserved names)
Permission rule syntax, sandbox settings, and settings keys that only take effect at some scopes
MEMORY.md load limits for subagent and auto memory, and the memory directory settings
irrelevant: Performance improvements, bug fixes that don't change config schema
CLI startup flags that don't touch files agnix reads

config_surfaces: .mcp.json or [mcp_servers.*] TOML blocks referenced from config.toml
relevant: New / renamed / removed keys in config.toml ([app], [agents], [features], [mcp_servers.*], [permissions], [sandbox], [windows], etc.)
Changes to MCP server schema (auth fields, bearer_token/env_var, allow-listed keys)
Feature toggles in [features] - new features, flag shapes (flat bool vs nested {enabled})
Plugin manifest schema changes in .codex-plugin/plugin.json or Agent Plugins root plugin.json
Per-client skill schema or .codex/skills directory layout changes
Apps config shape ([apps.*], tool-approval modes, default_tools_* keys)
Hook configuration schema (config.toml hooks block stabilized in 0.124)
AGENTS.md size limits, required sections, or directive grammar
hooks.json schema: hook event names, handler fields, timeouts, discovery locations
Custom agent TOML fields in .codex/agents/*.toml and the built-in agent names
Command rule (.rules) grammar: prefix_rule fields, decisions, justification
AGENTS.override.md precedence and the project_doc_max_bytes limit
Custom prompt deprecation, skills.max_context_tokens and agents/openai.yaml skill metadata
irrelevant: Model additions, reasoning presets, context-length bumps
TUI keyboard shortcuts and display tweaks
App-server plumbing, Unix socket transport, remote thread config

opencode.notes: OpenCode 1 line (npm opencode-ai, docs at https://opencode.ai/docs/). The repository moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode. OpenCode 2 ships from the same repository and is tracked separately as opencode-v2; release_tag_regex keeps this entry on the v1.X.Y GitHub releases even if a v2 release is ever marked latest. Validators are shared by both lines and gated by [tool_versions] opencode (rules with version_range <2.0.0 or >=2.0.0).

config_surfaces: CLAUDE.md (read only when no AGENTS.md exists)
opencode.json / opencode.jsonc (project, .opencode/, ~/.config/opencode/ and the system managed directory)
relevant: New / renamed / removed top-level keys in opencode.json or opencode.jsonc, including V1 keys deprecated in favor of OpenCode 2 forms
Permission config schema (including rule ordering semantics)
LSP config shape (request keys, permission-prompt payload)
MCP server definition shape / auth / env-var substitution rules
Markdown agent and command frontmatter, and plural vs legacy singular .opencode/ directory names
Custom tool and plugin module layout, and built-in tool names
Policies and references config
Per-client skill schema or .opencode/skills directory layout changes
AGENTS.md grammar or size limits
irrelevant: Model additions, provider plumbing, OAuth flow UI
Experimental HTTP API endpoints that don't change config files

opencode-v2.notes: OpenCode 2 line (npm @opencode/cli, docs at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, first release v2.0.0 on 2026-09-11). It is published as v2.X.Y git tags in anomalyco/opencode with no GitHub releases (on 2026-10-17 every GitHub release was v1.X.Y and releases/latest was v1.19.3), so the watcher finds no matching release and falls back to the tags API filtered by release_tag_regex; the issue body is then the tags-only stub and triage is skipped. Read the change via https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode/cli, the tag diff (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/compare/<baseline>...<new tag>) and https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/. Baseline v2.0.32 matches npm @opencode/cli latest and the v2 docs reviewed on 2026-10-17. Shares validators with opencode (OpenCode 1).

config_surfaces: opencode.json / opencode.jsonc (project, .opencode/, ~/.config/opencode/ and the system managed directory)
relevant: Native V2 config keys (agents, commands, permissions, plugins, providers, policies, references, snapshots, update, media) and V1 keys that V2 deprecates or ignores
permissions array shape, action names (shell, subagent, edit, external_directory) and rule ordering
Policy statement schema and precedence across config files
mcp.servers entry fields (enabled flag, snake_case OAuth fields, timeouts)
Agent and command Markdown frontmatter and V2 agent fields
Skill discovery, skill ID and frontmatter rules
AGENTS.md discovery and instruction files
Changes to V1 compatibility in the migration guide (opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)
irrelevant: Model additions, provider plumbing, OAuth flow UI
TUI and terminal settings in ~/.config/opencode/cli.json (not validated)
Server API, SDK and session-runner internals

kiro.notes: Proprietary CLI; no GH releases. Tracked via HTML scrape of kiro.dev/changelog/cli/ - the first NN.NN.NN version on the page is the latest. Release-note body is upgraded via GLM (scripts/glm-extract.js). The CLI itself exposes `kiro-cli version --changelog`. IDE has a separate changelog at https://kiro.dev/changelog/ide/ (not tracked here; could be added as a separate kiro-ide entry if needed).

config_surfaces: POWER.md, power plugin.json, power mcp.json, power steering/*.md
relevant: New / renamed CLI settings keys (writable via `kiro-cli settings <k> <v>`)
Steering file inclusion-mode or format changes
AGENTS.md steering discovery scope (2.18.0 loads nested AGENTS.md from anywhere in the workspace tree)
Agent definition schema (tools, permissions, auth)
Hook event names, payload shapes, required fields
MCP server config shape (auth, env substitution, tool filtering)
Power manifest schema
Skills directory layout or slash-command naming rules
Capability policy (permissions.yaml / permissions.json, managed-settings.json) schema
Workflow recipe schema in .kiro/workflows
.kiroignore syntax and locations

copilot.notes: Tracks the canonical VS Code Copilot Chat extension - the surface where new instruction-file features and schema changes typically land first. Note: the spec docs at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/customizing-copilot can change independently of extension releases; spec-drift.yml covers that path. The intermediate v0.43.{timestamp} CI tags are not flagged because the GitHub releases API returns the marked-latest stable tag.

relevant: Changes to instruction-file frontmatter, globs, or resolution order
New instruction-file naming conventions or scope rules
Additions to the supported instruction-file markdown directives
Changes to custom agent and reusable prompt frontmatter or file layout
Changes to Copilot hook events, hook configuration, or setup workflow conventions
Changes to Copilot skill frontmatter or the .github/skills directory layout
MCP server config inside custom agent files (mcp-servers, COPILOT_MCP_ secret names)
irrelevant: MCP / agent-mode features that don't touch the instruction-file surface

cline.notes: Tracks only the core Cline vX.Y.Z release train. The repository also publishes desktop-v*, cli-v*, sdk/*, and other interleaved releases that do not correspond to the validator surfaces.

relevant: Changes to .clinerules parsing (file vs dir, precedence)
Changes to .cline/rules Markdown discovery or conditional paths
New workflow/hook/skill file layouts
Skill frontmatter schema changes
Memory-bank format changes
.clineignore deprecation or removal
MCP server fields in cline_mcp_settings.json (type for remote servers)
irrelevant: cline-core internal diagnostics and memory tuning

cursor.notes: Tracked via Cursor's stable update endpoint (the same one the desktop app polls). Returns JSON like {"url":"...","name":"3.1.17"}. Channel is hardcoded to 'stable' for darwin; the version is platform-agnostic (same release ships across darwin/linux/win32). Prose changelog at https://cursor.com/changelog (Next.js SPA - not scrapeable from raw HTML).

relevant: Changes to .cursor/rules/**/*.mdc extension requirements or frontmatter (globs, description, alwaysApply)
New hook shapes in .cursor/hooks.json
Agent frontmatter schema in .cursor/agents/**/*.md
environment.json schema changes
MCP config shape inside .cursor/mcp.json
Per-client skill schema or .cursor/skills directory layout changes
Cursor CLI config and permissions.json allowlist schema
Plugin manifest and marketplace schema in .cursor-plugin/
.cursorignore pattern semantics
irrelevant: Agents Window UX (worktrees, multitask, subagents orchestration)

amp.notes: Tracked via the amp news RSS feed; the 'version' is the slug of the latest /news/ post (e.g., amp-free-is-ad-free). Source is not on GitHub; npm @sourcegraph/amp publishes per-commit (no semver gates) so npm version-bump tracking would be noise. Issue body uses the first <item><description> CDATA from the RSS feed (already structured HTML - no LLM needed).

relevant: New or renamed keys in .amp/settings.json (cli-settings.schema.json)
Changes to check frontmatter schema (name, description, severity-default)
Changes to AGENTS.md @-mentions or globs frontmatter in mentioned files
Changes to skill roots, discovery depth or precedence, and skill MCP fields (mcp.json, mcpServers, includeTools)
Changes to amp.mcpPermissions or ${amp:id-token} handling
Changes to .gemini/settings.json top-level keys
Agent markdown frontmatter schema (kind, mcp_servers block, auth variants, system_prompt)
gemini-extension.json manifest shape
GEMINI.md grammar / size limits / import syntax
Hook env vars and plan-mode directives that affect agent files
Custom command TOML fields (prompt, description) and {{args}}, !{...}, @{...} injection syntax
Policy engine TOML rule schema and policy file locations
Hook events, matchers and timeout units in settings.json and extension hooks/hooks.json
MCP server fields in settings.json and gemini-extension.json (transport, trust)

windsurf.notes: Proprietary IDE (Codeium/Exafunction); no GH releases. Tracked via HTML scrape of windsurf.com/changelog - the first 'Wave NN' marker on the page is the latest. Release-note body is upgraded via GLM (scripts/glm-extract.js). Wave is the marketing release event; underlying VS Code-fork build version (e.g., 1.9544.24) bumps more often but is not the agnix-relevant signal. Separate /vscode, /jetbrains, /windsurf-next channels are not tracked.

config_surfaces: ~/.codeium/hooks.json and system hooks.json (Devin and Windsurf admin directories)
relevant: New rules or workflows file layout / frontmatter (trigger values, globs, description)
Rule, workflow and global_rules.md character limits
Legacy .windsurf/ and .windsurfrules deprecation status
Cascade hook events, hook options and hooks.json locations
Workflow support in the Devin Local agent
Any new per-project config file under .devin/ or .windsurf/

agentskills-spec.notes: The agentskills.io Skill specification (the generic cross-tool SKILL.md standard) - the source for agnix's AS-* rules. It publishes NO releases or tags, so it is tracked by the latest commit SHA touching docs/specification.mdx in the agentskills/agentskills repo (commit_repo + commit_path source). Any change opens an issue to diff the spec against the AS-* rules. Complements the weekly spec-drift.yml check. last_known_version is the short commit SHA.

config_surfaces: SKILL.md frontmatter (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools)
relevant: Changed field constraints (description max length, name format, compatibility limit)
New / renamed / removed frontmatter fields
allowed-tools value-shape changes (string vs list)
Body / file-reference rules
irrelevant: Prose / example wording edits with no normative change
